10.1103/627p-l6zk.abstract: Ferrimagnetic skyrmions offer enhanced tunability due to antiferromagnetically coupled sublattices and reduced net magnetization. In chiral magnetic films at zero magnetic field, skyrmion stability is commonly characterized by a dimensionless parameter $κ$, yet its applicability to ferrimagnetic systems remains unclear, as most studies assume a fixed, strong inter-sublattice exchange coupling $J$. Here we investigate how variations in $J$ govern relaxed stable and metastable ferrimagnetic skyrmion configurations and introduce a dimensionless parameter $ζ_{eff}$ to characterize the crossover between strong and weak inter-sublattice locking. In the strong-coupling regime, inter-sublattice locking enables stabilization of skyrmion in a sublattice where intrinsic Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction is absent while the other sublattice has finite DMI, yielding a sublattice with DMI-free ferrimagnetic skyrmions. As $J$ decreases, this locking breaks down, leading to independent sublattice behavior and the failure of an effective $κ$-based description. Our results establish a unified framework linking inter-sublattice exchange and skyrmion phase stability in ferrimagnetic systems.
10.1103/627p-l6zk.title: Generic skyrmion phase diagram in ferrimagnetic films

10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174602.abstract: k π -skyrmions are topological magnetic textures with promising applications in spintronic devices. In this work, we investigated the stability and current-driven dynamics of k π -skyrmions ( k = 1,2,3 , and 4) in racetrack nanostructures. Stability phase diagrams were constructed as a function of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction strength ( D int ) and the perpendicular magnetic field ( B z ). Our results showed that the stabilization range of each k π -skyrmion strongly depends on D int . In addition, the diameters of all textures increased with increasing D int and decreased with increasing B z . The current-driven dynamics induced by spin–orbit torque were then investigated. Our results showed that the velocity of all k π -skyrmions increased with current density and decreased with perpendicular magnetic field. Although the 3 π -skyrmion exhibited larger longitudinal velocities during the transient regime than the π -skyrmion, both textures reached nearly identical steady-state velocities. A similar behavior was observed for the 2 π - and 4 π -skyrmions. The steady-state dynamics were further analyzed using the Thiele formalism, which reproduced the trends observed in the micromagnetic simulations. These findings provide insight into the stabilization and transport properties of k π -skyrmions and support their potential use in future spintronic applications.
10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174602.title: Spin orbit torque manipulation of kπ-skyrmions in racetrack nanostructures for spintronic memory applications

10.1021/acsnano.6c10331.abstract: Abstract Heterostructures of 2D materials offer high tunability of magnetic properties, including current-induced magnetization switching by unconventional spin–orbit torques. The microscopic mechanisms governing spin-torque switching in van der Waals systems, however, remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate current-induced magnetization reversal in an Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) and WTe2 heterostructure using scanning harmonic magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy. Spatially resolved magnetization maps show that field-free switching unfolds from asymmetric domain nucleation at the edges of the FGT flake, followed by domain wall propagation. This switching behavior is deterministic and bipolar, consistent with spin–orbit torques arising from the injection of both in-plane and out-of-plane spins from WTe2 into FGT. The critical currents for up-to-down and down-to-up switching differ because of asymmetric domain nucleation and directional domain wall pinning effects. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the switching behavior observed experimentally, showing how the initial domain nucleation sites are determined by the sample geometry and combined influence of in-plane and out-of-plane spins and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Finally, by systematically varying the field-like and damping-like torque components and sweeping the spin polarization between in-plane and out-of-plane, we identify the torque configurations that yield the most efficient switching in van der Waals magnets with different shapes.
10.1021/acsnano.6c10331.title: Unfolding of Field-Free Spin–Orbit Torque Magnetization Switching in a van der Waals Heterostructure

10.1088/1361-648x/aeb217.abstract: Abstract Since its experimental discovery as an intrinsic antiferromagnetic topological insulator in 2019, the MnBi 2 Te 4 family of materials has greatly propelled the development of condensed matter physics over the past several years. This family naturally integrates long-range magnetic order with topological band structure within a two-dimensional van der Waals layered material, providing an unprecedentedly clean platform for exploring quantum phenomena such as axion insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and the topological magnetoelectric effect. However, the transition from fundamental research to practical applications, particularly the realization of high-temperature quantum effects, is confronted with severe challenges in intrinsic defects, magnetic ground-state tuning, and electronic structure engineering. This article aims to review the current development status of the MnBi 2 Te 4 family, focusing on its core quantum phenomena, recent revolutionary breakthroughs in sample preparation techniques, and diverse tuning methods. On this basis, we outline possible pathways toward high-temperature quantum effects through innovations in material synthesis, interface engineering, and multi-strategy tuning and heterostructure engineering.
10.1088/1361-648x/aeb217.title: The challenging path toward high-temperature quantum anomalous hall effect in MnBi 2 Te 4

10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174616.abstract: The anomalous Hall conductivity of the bulk ferrimagnetic Heusler alloy Mn 2 PtSn is calculated using density functional theory combined with maximally localized Wannier functions. The corresponding Berry curvature distributions are then computed, from which the net anomalous Hall conductivity is obtained. To enhance the anomalous Hall conductivity through symmetry reduction, three energetically stable (001) surface terminations of Mn 2 PtSn are considered, and their Berry curvature distributions are compared with those of the bulk unit cell. The increased number of Berry curvature peaks at the surface terminations leads to a higher value of the anomalous Hall conductivity. The anomalous Hall conductivity is also evaluated as a function of the Fermi level, and the presence of sharp peaks near the Fermi level indicates the potential for further enhancement through Fermi-level tuning. The high value of anomalous Hall conductivity at the surfaces highlights their potential for application in thin-film memory devices, where surface-driven properties are crucial. • Anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) of bulk and (001) Mn 2 PtSn surfaces is calculated. • Surface-induced symmetry-breaking enhances the AHC. • The Pt full monolayer shows the enhanced Berry curvature and AHC due to strong spin–orbit interaction. • AHC peak near Fermi level suggests potential for further AHC enhancement via tuning.
10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174616.title: Surface-enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity in ferrimagnetic Mn2PtSn Heusler alloy
